statement: status and manuscript converge after a merge. Two independent derivations run over one log — status is the single latest LIFECYCLE op by opId, text is a fold of every op's changes in opId order — and nothing made them agree, so a reject beating an already-spliced accept settled `rejected` with the suggestion still in the manuscript, permanently (neither reject nor reopen could move text). The post-merge pass now appends a `claudeReject` carrying the INVERSE changes, stamped `synthesisSource = .rejectConvergence` and carrying the winning reject's userResponse: one op that is both the newest lifecycle op (status stays rejected) and the newest changes-carrying op (the text goes back). `Deriver.appliesToManuscript` admits `.claudeReject` for this and only this — every writer-issued reject still carries empty changes — and ProjectManifest.currentSchemaVersion went 4→5 because an older build folds none of it. Idempotent: once the repair is the newest payload the detection is false, so two devices repairing the same race cannot ping-pong. DECLINES loudly when the paragraph has drifted since the accept, leaving the disagreement visible rather than writing over the writer's own sentences. WAITS while the piece is unsettled (#84, Denver's ruling (a), 2026-10-19): where the stamp carries `localWritePermit.unsettledStarter` — a book author's hand in a piece somebody else started and nobody has claimed — the repair writes nothing, because its text would CLAIM the piece in the author's name and set the starter's held words aside on every Mac. The disagreement stands visibly and loses nothing; the trigger persists, so a later merge repairs it once the stamp has settled (not the merge that brings the claim — DocumentStore re-stamps after handleExternalLogChange)

scope: Document.declineUndo — the annotation undos' drift declines
statement: One ⌘Z over a COALESCED batch reports its declines in ONE sentence carrying the count; a single decline reads exactly as it always has. The bulk bar registers one undo closure per note and `NSUndoManager.groupsByEvent` folds them into a single event group (pinned by `AnnotationBulkActionsTests`), and each closure re-checks its own note at fire time and declines out loud when it drifted (RULING-22, M5-AN-019's shape). Before this every declining closure called `notifyWriter` directly, so N drifted notes posted the SINGULAR sentence N times into a toast slot that renders one (`RewindModifier`'s `restoreToast = message`): the writer read 'Couldn't undo stetting the note' — false about the number, and silent about the notes that DID undo. The four decline sites (the annotation edit, the textless accept, the stet, the triage mark) now call `Document.declineUndo(_:)`, which accumulates per `UndoDecline` verb and spends one sentence a main-actor hop after the last of the batch's undo closures — RULING-32's sweep shape (`_sweptSinceLastReport`, spent at the burst boundary) applied to the same problem one column over. The boundary needs no timer: every sibling closure's task is enqueued before the report task is created, and a declining closure never suspends. Each verb's singular and plural sentences sit on adjacent lines in `UndoDecline`, and the singular is byte-identical to what each site posted before — the single-note decline tests are the proof. A batch that declined some notes and undid others says nothing about the successes: the queue holds the reopened rows. The accumulator has a FIFTH caller that is not a refusal: the put-back's failure (`UndoDecline.putBack`, M5-AN-060/069 — stet's, reject's and archive's undos), which reports through the same boundary for the same reason — one ⌘Z, one sentence — and is why `UndoDecline` is the set of things an annotation undo can have to say rather than the set of verbs it can refuse

statement: The reject and archive undos re-check, at fire time and from an UNFILTERED query, that the note still shows the status this action wrote (`.rejected` / `.archived`) before they reopen it; on drift they append nothing and DECLINE OUT LOUD through `Document.declineUndo(.reject)` / `(.archive)` — "Couldn't undo rejecting the note — it changed on another device." / "Couldn't undo archiving the note — it changed on another device." statement: A note on a table figure anchors by row and column id and the deriver resolves it against the figure's table: it follows inserts (figureAddress is the current A1), and it is stale and orphaned when any corner's row or column is deleted, live again when the delete is undone. statement: One ⌘Z undoes one decision. Before this (#128 item 1) both undos ended in a bare `reopenAnnotation(id:)`, which only ever yields `.open`, so one ⌘Z discarded the new answer AND the earlier one. The fire-time drift guard and its loud decline are unchanged (M5-AN-062); a put-back that fails after the reopen landed says `declineUndo(.putBack)`. `AnnotationInverse.reopenOp` and `reopenAnnotation(id:)` are untouched (tripwire 19; M5-AN-034/040)

scope: Research note and palette card versions — when one is kept
statement: A Research note or palette card (a text item in Research whose path sits inside a research root — research/ or a loose piece's own research/ folder, no path component starting with '.'; a card is one under the palette folder, and cards keep versions since Denver's 2026-11-11 answer to P2) keeps earlier versions under .maugham/research-versions/<itemId>/, the last 50 per item per device: the writer's own typing — in the note editor, or the card editor's own saves (updatePaletteCard(typed: true)) — keeps ONE version per editing run (saves less than 10 minutes apart are one run — the text before the run), and every other writer of a note's or card's text ALWAYS keeps what it replaced and ends the run — a canvas Rewrite (which lands only if that version was kept, and leaves no Trash entry, M6-PR-037) or link append, a canvas or inbox promotion into a card (the assistant's promote_inbox_entry marked as replaced by the assistant), a wiki-link rename sweep, Search & Replace, an asset-reference rewrite after a rename or move, a Restore, and the assistant's update_note (notes only); a change made to the file outside Maugham is kept at the next save. Anything else (a table, picture, PDF, or a text item whose path is outside a research root, such as the manuscript or a .maugham/ file) is refused by the door and keeps nothing. Wherever the project's window store is open (every production writer), a note's or card's text is written only through the door — the palette funnel (paletteCoordinatedWrite) included, and every card writer reaches it; with no document store (a load-only context) the rename sweep, Replace, a promotion and the palette funnel write raw and keep no version; and, like the table door, no writer writes anything whose path is outside a research root. When anyone else's write of a card cannot keep its version, it is refused (updatePaletteCard throws researchTextNotSaved, the card is as it was, and the door says why); the card editor's own save lands with the notice, as a note's flush does. A canvas Rewrite of a text item or card outside a research root is refused before anything is read or written. When a version cannot be kept, a timed autosave is not made and the writer is told once; a save at a note switch, close, ⌘S or a move is made anyway with a notice that the earlier version could not be kept (interim behaviour, not yet ruled). A file that will not read is never saved over. A timed autosave that is not made — its version cannot be kept, its file will not read, or its write fails — leaves the edit pending and says so once. A save at a note switch, close or ⌘S whose file will not read, or whose write fails, keeps the typed text as a conflict backup under .maugham/conflicts/ and names it in the notice; when that backup cannot be written either, the notice says the edits were not saved. An edit whose note has left Research, stopped being a note, or whose path the project refuses is not dropped either: a timed autosave keeps it pending and the save at a note switch, close or ⌘S keeps it as a conflict backup and names it. A writer that reads a note to rewrite it waits for any save of that note already in flight, so it never writes text made from older bytes over the writer's edit.

statement: A checkpoint revert of a figure answers its notes by ONE walk (`FigureRestoreNotePlan`, Core; the figure twin of `RewindImpact.travelStatusChanges`) with three classes, and a note is changed only where the revert rewrites its cell. STRANDED (accepted now, not accepted at the checkpoint pointer, its cell rewritten): the cell change IS the note's `claudeAcceptRevert` (cell and note in one op) and the note reopens. RETURNING (open after a Revert, accepted at the pointer, the restore writes its accepted value back): the cell change becomes a `claudeAccept` carrying the note, checkpoint-stamped, and the note returns to ACCEPTED (RULING-57 for figures). GONE (its row or column does not exist at the checkpoint): `claudeArchive`, status only, or a status-only reopen where this hand may not dispose. A note on a cell the restore does not write keeps its status, and so does a note accepted at the pointer and now (R-A, RULING-58). A revived row or column counts as written, at the value the revive gives each live cell: a stranded note there gets a status-only revert, a returning one a status-only accept. A stranded note whose cell the restore writes to that note's OWN suggested content stays accepted, whether by a cell set or a revive (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). Where two stranded notes share the written cell the change carries the note with the newest cell-carrying accept and the other gets a status-only revert (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). A guarded-accepted note (status-only accept, no cell-carrying accept after the pointer; M5-AN-075) is judged by its anchor cell and suggested content: it IS stranded where the restore writes its cell away from the suggestion (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver; this overrules the design spec's section 3 sentence that such a note is never stranded). A restore that stops part way and is retried writes one accept for a returning note, not two.

statement: The revert sheet counts a figure's notes BEFORE the revert and the result sentence reports them AFTER from the same plan: `FigureDocument.restoreNotesPreview` runs the restore's own preparation (`FigureCheckpointRestore.prepare`, one copy) and returns the plan's notes (reopened, returned to accepted, archived) while writing nothing (no op, no annotations-changed event, `lastRestoreNotes` untouched). Each figure is counted through `PartialRestorePicker.reach`, the one function the revert also uses to gate a figure (in scope, a pointer in the checkpoint, the settled posture allows editing), so a parked, refused, went-to-Research or out-of-scope figure is in no count, and counting leaves a figure that was open open, and leaves no host open that it borrowed. Both halves share one counting phrase per class ('N accepted suggestion(s)' reopened or archived, 'N suggestion(s)' restored to accepted). Confirm: 'N accepted suggestion(s) will be reopened on A.', 'N suggestion(s) will be restored to accepted on A.', 'N accepted suggestion(s) will be archived on A — its cell is gone then.'; result: 'Reopened … restored … and archived …'. A restore stopped part way reports what landed; the preview names the whole plan.

statement: Where the cell's content already is the suggestion's content (format and alignment aside), Accept marks the note accepted and writes nothing to the cell: one status-only `claudeAccept` (`figure == nil`, `FigureAnnotationOps.statusOnlyAccept`). The check runs after every existing refusal and after the changed-since check, and `confirmChanged` makes no difference. No accept in the log ever records `prior == next` (RULING-59), including after the race that leaves a note open over its own value (a peer's reject, then a reopen). Its ⌘Z, in or out of a grid visit, is a status-only `claudeAcceptRevert` that reopens the note and moves no cell (`Change.statusOnly`); ⇧⌘Z accepts again, guarded again. The ⌘Z and ⇧⌘Z (and the visit's undo and redo) DECLINE, writing nothing, once the cell has changed or its row is gone. A restore may strand a guarded accept (M5-AN-073).

statement: Accept of a suggested change writes a status-only `claudeAccept` (no changes) in exactly these cases: (1) the note's newest text-carrying `claudeAccept` is for the note's paragraph and its `next` is the live paragraph, even when the span's quote no longer resolves; (2) the note's own history says its splice is live and the replacement stands, aligned, around the quote occurrence the span's anchor resolves to in the live paragraph. 'Live' is a fold over the note's honoured lifecycle lines in opId order: an accept opens it; a text-carrying revert or RULING-33 repair closes it; a status-only revert or reopen written by Maugham's own travel (stamped `.rewind` or `.undoRewind`, or with a checkpoint) closes it; every other line, every archive (a travel's own too) and every other status-only line leaves it unchanged (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver for the fold's travel arms and for a span whose splice is still in the text being accepted status-only where it used to refuse as anchor-lost); (3) the paragraph already equals the computed result (the whole-paragraph hand-typed case). Otherwise Accept splices as before, or refuses as anchor-lost (RULING-5); a span whose quote is gone while its splice is NOT in place still refuses. So a suggestion is never spliced twice and no accept records a before-text equal to its after-text (RULING-59): after another device's newer archive or stet and a Reopen, after a restore that put the splice back following a Revert, after an edit elsewhere in the paragraph. After the writer's Revert, and after Maugham's own travel took the splice out (a rewind to before the accept, a rewind that removed the paragraph followed by a return journey, a checkpoint revert), Accept splices again. After the writer's reopen-only Revert of a hand-typed accept it is status-only again. The status-only accept's ⌘Z is an `annotationReopen` that leaves the text, declined once another device moved the note, and ⇧⌘Z re-accepts, guarded again; Revert restores the original (coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver). Mac and phone decide it in one Core function (tripwire 19). Known limits: (L1) the span reading follows the anchor resolver's choice of quote occurrence; (L2) a hand-typed SPAN suggestion on a never-accepted note is spliced as written; (L3) the race (accept → peer archive/stet → pane Reopen, note open over its splice) → a rewind that removes the paragraph → a RETURN JOURNEY (not ⌘Z) to a point after the accept, whose step 9 writes a `.rewind` reopen → an edit elsewhere in the paragraph → Accept, with a replacement that contains its quote: the gate is closed and the suggestion is spliced a second time. Four conditions including a cross-device race; the result is visible and ⌘Z takes it back (a documented limit, not pinned by a test; coordinator's call, hardening 2026-11-11, not yet ruled by Denver).

statement: A note created on a figure while a checkpoint restore of that figure is running does NOT stop the restore: the open host adopts the already-signed note op in place (`FigureDocument.adoptNoteCreation`) and does not advance `reloadGeneration`, so the restore's generation check passes. The host holds the note and it is on disk. The restore ends `.restored`, not `.partlyRestored(.changedElsewhere)`; a RELOAD mid-restore still stops it and a retry finishes.
